s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of respiratory and skin symptoms with a progressive rash
salient_findings: Pseudovesicular papules with superficial crusting on the trunk
key_facts: Age of the patient is in the 60s
Initial symptoms include asthenia, anorexia, and cough
Hospitalization occurred six days after symptom onset
Papules were asymptomatic and measured 3- to 6-mm
Papules evolved to a purpuric rash within 48 hours
Nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR tests for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 were negative
Immunohistochemical testing for herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses was negative
RT-PCR testing of fixed skin tissue for SARS-CoV-2 was negative
Histologic analysis showed extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis
Large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration were present
Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis

shortlist.label: Toxic epidermal necrolysis
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis and large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration

shortlist.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive rash with purpuric evolution and mucocutaneous involvement suggested by systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Papulovesicular eruption with superficial crusting and rapid progression to purpuric rash

shortlist.label: Erythema multiforme
shortlist.why_kept: Targetoid lesions not explicitly mentioned but possible given the description of papulovesicular eruption and purpuric rash

shortlist.label: Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Early-stage vasculitic alterations with endothelial swelling of dermal vessels and perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate

raw.rationale: The presence of extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis, large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration, and the evolution of papules to a purpuric rash are consistent with toxic epidermal necrolysis, which is a severe skin condition usually triggered by medications or infections.

rejected.label: Stevens-Johnson syndrome
rejected.why: While similar to toxic epidermal necrolysis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome typically involves less than 10% of the body surface area and often includes mucosal involvement, which is not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome
rejected.why: This condition is more common in children and is caused by staphylococcal toxins, which is not indicated in the case.

rejected.label: Erythema multiforme
rejected.why: Erythema multiforme is characterized by target lesions, which are not described in the case, and it often involves mucosal surfaces.

rejected.label: Vasculitis
rejected.why: While there are some vasculitic alterations mentioned, the primary findings suggest a more severe epidermal process, such as toxic epidermal necrolysis, rather than a primary vasculitis.
